Hi Samir / Alyssa —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. I focused this note on the technical constraints and the goals we heard from your architecture and ops teams.

Summary of pain & goals
- Latency: production SLO target is P95 < 120ms for typical 512-token responses (some prompts ~256 tokens). P50 ideally < 60ms.
- Throughput: steady-state ~80 req/s, expected bursts up to 250 req/s for short windows during shifts.
- Model requirements: clinical-safe answers, hallucination controls, and token-limited context for patient histories (avg session length ~1,800 tokens). Primary model: latest open 70B family (fine-tune likely) with a fall-back 13B for low-cost routing.
- Deployment constraints: on-prem / VPC-only deployment is required for PHI. Cardinal needs KMS integration and 1-year audit log retention.
- Reliability: multi-zone failover within a single region; optional cross-region fallback for business continuity.

Key technical implications we discussed
- KV / prefix caching will materially reduce token cost and latency given repeated patient-context prefixes. We should measure hit-rates during the PoC.
- Quantized model variants (int8 / 4-bit) are attractive for throughput but must be validated against your quality regressions.
- Routing strategy: low-latency tier for critical flows (p95 budget) and cost tier for best-effort or background tasks (13B).

Attached: initial topology sketch and an empty SLO matrix (cardinal-topology-draft.pdf, slo-matrix.csv).

Asks / next steps
1) Please confirm the operational constraints above (latency, throughput, retention) or flag anything I missed.
2) Share a short sample of production traces (anonymized) or a representative prompt mix — this will help our sizing and batch/latency modeling.
3) We'd like to schedule a focused PoC week (3–5 days) to validate p95 latency with a quantized 70B variant in a Cardinal VPC. Is the week of Nov 29 workable?
4) We will produce a concrete topology proposal and a recommended GPU count by Friday (2026-11-13).

If anything above needs correction, tell me and I'll update the doc. Otherwise Jordan will follow up with a detailed topology and sizing rationale.

Thanks,

Samir / team —

Following Irene's summary, here's a technical deep-dive and a concrete topology proposal. I put numbers we can validate in the PoC; these are conservative starting estimates.

Topology (private / VPC)
- Deployment mode: Redwood Private (customer VPC control plane) with dedicated GPU pool inside Cardinal network.
- Node type: H100 80GB GPUs for the low-latency tier (70B int4 / optimized kernels), fallback tier with A100 80GB or q4_0 13B variant for cost-sensitive traffic.
- Routing: request router with policy rules:
  - Route A (critical): 70B-int4 on H100, single-request priority, adaptive batching disabled for critical flows (batch size=1, target concurrency isolation). p50/p95 estimates below.
  - Route B (cost): 13B-q4 with adaptive batching (batch window 5–15ms), used for background processes and low-priority sessions.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache per-session with hot-shard replication. Expect hit-rate uplift if session reuse > 20%.
- High availability: 3 AZ spread within region, stateful failover for KV cache, fallback route to secondary pool in case of capacity saturations.

Sizing & perf estimates (ballpark for PoC validation)
- Workload: average response length 512 tokens, 80 req/s steady-state, bursts up to 250 req/s for <10min.
- Observed (estimated) latencies — single-request (no batching):
  - 70B int4 on H100: p50 ~48ms, p95 ~112ms for 512-token responses (includes model decode).
  - 13B q4 on A100: p50 ~26ms, p95 ~70ms for 512-token responses.
- Throughput per GPU (sustained, mixed-workload estimate):
  - H100 (70B int4): ~30–40 req/s steady at p95 budget.
  - A100 (13B q4): ~120–150 req/s with batching.
- GPU count recommendation (initial) for steady-state 80 rps with headroom:
  - Low-latency pool (H100, 70B): 3 GPUs (covers ~90–120 rps with p95 headroom; helps absorb bursts when combined with routing rules).
  - Cost pool (A100 / 13B): 1–2 GPUs for background traffic and overflow.
- Burst strategy: enable short-term burst capacity via preemptible nodes or a small buffer of warm GPUs; fallback to 13B for overflow to keep p95 within budget.

Operational & security notes
- KMS/HSM: Redwood Private supports BYOK via customer KMS — we'll collect key ARNs and access boundaries during PoC onboarding.
- Audit/log retention: we can route request/response metadata to your SIEM with one-year retention; full-response logging must be gated for PHI.
- Compliance: we'll provide SOC2 artifacts and our security questionnaire; Marissa will lead the security intake.

Next deliverables from Redwood (due 2026-11-13)
- Complete topology PDF (attached: cardinal-topology-draft.pdf)
- Populated SLO matrix with formulae and baseline estimates (slo-matrix.csv)
- PoC runbook: traffic generator config, sample prompts, and success criteria (latency & quality checks).

Open questions for PoC prep
1) Will you allow telemetry for token-level timing for PoC? This helps validate p95 budgeting.
2) Do you have a preferred KMS provider/ARN to test with?
3) Is there an existing NATS/Redis instance we should integrate for session KV or should we stand up a PoC replica?

I'll attach the brief topology sketch and a blank SLO matrix to this thread. We can iterate quickly.

—Jordan
